ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act Articles 287 et seq. (Yuhan Hoesa); Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (as amended); Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act; Act on Regulation of Concealment of Crime Proceeds; Financial Services Commission AML/CFT guidelines; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit UBO identification decrees; and the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or corporate registrar in the foreign parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention member, the certificate must receive an apostille from the designated competent authority and then be filed directly with Korean authorities without consular legalization. If the issuing jurisdiction is not a member, the certificate must be authenticated by the local ministry of foreign affairs and then legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate in that jurisdiction. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive parallel paths and must never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registrar or corporate registry authority in the foreign parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague member states, attach the apostille issued by the competent authority and present directly to Korean registry, tax and bank reviewers. For non-member states, complete local authentication followed by Korean consular legalization. Apostille route and consular route are alternatives; sequential chaining is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the Korean incorporation agent and bank account signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign parent entity, certified by a licensed notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The notarized resolution and power of attorney must be apostilled if the executing jurisdiction is a member of the Hague Convention and then used directly for Korean filings. For non-member jurisdictions, after notarization the document must be authenticated and then submitted for Korean consular legalization. The two authentication routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; do not chain apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or equivalent constitutional documents of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent entity and its corporate secretary, evidenced by notarial certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authenticate under the apostille procedure for convention jurisdictions or under Korean consular legalization for non-convention jurisdictions. Apostille and consular jurisdiction are alternative procedures based on treaty membership; no document may pass through both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the foreign parent entity's principal bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal relationship or corporate banking institution of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: the bank letter must be certified by a notary public and then apostilled by the relevant competent authority of the contracting state before submission to Korean financial institutions. Non-Hague route: the certified letter must be authenticated by the local foreign affairs authority and then legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate. These paths are mutually exclusive; concatenation is invalid.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, officers, authorized signatories, commercial partners and payment-rail beneficiaries must be screened before incorporation and on a continuous basis against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, European Union consolidated sanctions lists, Republic of Korea individual sanctions notifications, Interpol notices and World Bank debarment lists. A domestic and foreign politically exposed person determination must be performed for government, judicial and military officials, their close associates and family members. Enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval are required for any PEP relationship, high-risk jurisdiction, adverse media hit, or any person holding 25 percent or more direct or indirect ownership. All screening results must be documented in Korean and retained for at least five years after termination of the relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (I-ROSa) Commercial Registry electronic search and filing portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be entered in Hangul in the articles of incorporation and the registration application. A foreign brand or trading name must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul following the National Institute of Korean Language transliteration standards. The four-tier name convention comprises a distinctive identifier, a business-object description, the statutory legal form and the mandatory limited-liability suffix Yuhan Hoesa. Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered trade name or a registered trademark are prohibited.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within seven days of rejection, the applicant must request a written statement of the registry grounds. The applicant may then file a formal objection with the commercial registry of the competent district court and, if necessary, an immediate appeal under the non-contentious registration procedure, ultimately to the Supreme Court. The appeal dossier must contain the corrected Hangul name, revised articles of incorporation, fresh trademark and name search results, and a cover letter explaining how the conflicts were removed. Because the Korean system does not maintain a separate administrative name-reservation extension, the applicant may immediately re-file a new name after clearance; administrative litigation remains available to contest a final rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox-only address is rejected by the National Tax Service and Korean commercial banks for a digital-store publisher because the Commercial Act requires a physical registered place of business and the VAT and corporate income tax regimes require accessible premises for inspection and service of process. The registered office must be a real non-residential space where the company manages Steam/PlayStation store agreements, keeps accounting books and records, stores corporate seals and license documentation, and maintains staff. A virtual office may supplement as a mailing address only and cannot replace the physical registered office for bank onboarding or tax registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: maintain a full-time manager or responsible director; post a nameplate and signage; keep the lease agreement, utility bills and floor plan on site; retain VAT invoices, corporate tax records and accounting ledgers at the registered address; maintain operating telephone and email; and ensure the premises are staffed during business hours. Quantified risk: for a low-risk standard Yuhan Hoesa LLC in Seoul, the likelihood of an unannounced National Tax Service or registry inspection in the first two years is estimated at 10 to 20 percent; if the company uses a virtual, shared, or sub-registered office, the estimated likelihood rises to 65 to 80 percent upon bank filing of a suspicious transaction report or VAT refund trigger.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (I-ROSa)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No government fee for the public name-search portal; counsel name-clearance work is included in the formation flat fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation registration fee and registration tax for Yuhan Hoesa LLC
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: District Court Registry Office and local tax office at the registered office location
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tax of 0.4 percent of stated capital, education tax surcharge and court registration fee under the Local Tax Act and Court Fees Act; estimate based on planned authorized capital base.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business registration certificate and VAT and corporate tax employer registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: National Tax Service and relevant local tax office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee; filings prepared as part of the legal formation package.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille or consular legalization of the parent corporate bundle including certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, board resolution and power of attorney, articles of association and bank reference letter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in the parent jurisdiction; competent ministry of foreign affairs; Korean Embassy or Consulate for consular legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff and official apostille fee; Korean consular legalization fee schedule where applicable.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing, PEP and international sanctions screening and enhanced due diligence report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Korean AML/CFT counsel and KYC data provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market flat fee for a standard low-risk LLC formation with five beneficial owner verification files and consolidated screening output.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered physical office procurement deposit and first-month rent in the Seoul metropolitan area
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Landlord and licensed real estate brokerage
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Seoul Grade-B office market benchmark; lease deposit refundable at term, one month advance rent and brokerage commission included.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, January 27, 1962, as last amended), Chapter on the Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), Article 287 and successive articles; together with the Commercial Registration Act of the Republic of Korea and the Supreme Court Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registry Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; online application portal: Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (Articles of Association) together with the Application for Registration of Incorporation filed with the Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act imposes no minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. The Articles of Incorporation must state the total stated capital and each member's contribution units. Cash contributions must be paid to a bank before incorporation, and the bank's Contribution Payment Certificate must be submitted to the Registry Office. There is no blocked escrow account requirement. In-kind contributions require a factual or independent valuation according to the in-kind contribution valuation rule of the Commercial Act; no escrow is prescribed. The registry's filing fee is expressed as USD 0 in this normalized schema because the actual amount is a registration license tax of 0.4 percent of the stated capital plus a local education surtax and a court fee, determined by the Registry at filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the founding members of YUHANGHOESA have agreed to incorporate as a Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and have executed and notarized the Articles of Incorporation; and WHEREAS the Articles of Incorporation state an aggregate initial contribution of [Total Capital Amount] Korean won allocated into units subscribed by each founding member, and the bank deposit receipt proves that subscription funds have been paid in full; NOW THEREFORE the Board of Directors, acting as the first board after organization, resolves unanimously as follows: 1. Share Capital Subscription. The Board ratifies, accepts and records the initial subscription statement of every founding member, and directs the secretary to enter in the company's ledger the number of contribution units issued to each member. The contribution payment certificate issued by [Depository Bank] shall be retained as a permanent corporate record. 2. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the company is adopted as [Street Address, city, province], Republic of Korea. All official notices, writs, registry mailings, tax notifications and other statutory correspondence shall be directed to this address, and the directors are authorized to sign lease or shared-office agreements necessary to maintain the registered office. 3. Banking Authorization. The Board establishes the corporate banking mandate and authorizes the Representative Director to open, operate and control bank accounts in the company's name, including United States dollar, Korean won and other settlement accounts required to receive Steam Valve payout, PlayStation Store payout and other digital distribution revenues. The Representative Director may sign account opening forms, mandate cards, wire transfer instructions and foreign exchange declarations with such banks, and may appoint one additional internal director

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, electronic portal HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); export clearance and customs validation are supported by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Yuhan Hoesa (Korean LLC), the statutory Tax Identification Number is the 10-digit Business Registration Number issued by the NTS district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered business address. Procedure: (1) prepare the Articles of Incorporation, business place lease evidence, director or shareholder passport identification, and company seal; (2) file an online Business Registration Application with HomeTax within 20 days of commencing the game publishing business; (3) receive the NTS Business Registration Certificate, which serves as VAT ID, corporate TIN, and e-tax invoice issuer ID. For a foreign non-resident vendor with no Korean registered place of business but making taxable supplies into Korea, the same HomeTax platform is used to apply as a foreign entrepreneur under the Value-Added Tax Act; the foreign entity must submit a power of attorney and appoint a Korean tax representative if no domestic fixed establishment exists, together with a foreign corporate certificate (apostilled or consularized), articles of incorporation, and evidence of Steam and PlayStation Store distribution contracts. NTS will assign a separate foreign business registration number; ongoing compliance requires the foreign supplier to file VAT electronically and maintain a local KRW payment account for tax collection.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the Yuhan Hoesa is a resident corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and is taxable on its worldwide income; it is not an eligible pass-through entity).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or elective tax classification regime in Korea. Classification follows legal form under the Commercial Act. Hybrid mismatch adjustments are made only under the Adjustment of International Tax Act, and no elective hybrid mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold for corporate taxpayers: any person supplying taxable goods or services in the Republic of Korea is required to register for VAT. Taxpayers other than corporations with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000 may qualify for simplified taxable person filing, but that status does not eliminate the registration duty; the Yuhan Hoesa is outside the simplified category because it is an incorporated entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoicing is mandatory for all registered businesses. Tax invoices must be issued as HomeTax e-tax invoices and transmitted to NTS through the HomeTax portal, NTS certified integration, or the official HomeTax open API; the e-tax invoice carries a nationally issued invoice number and digital signature code matched by NTS with VAT returns, customs declarations, and bank statements. NTS performs near-real-time cross-matching of e-tax invoice data, cash receipt declarations, export cargo records, and foreign exchange receipts. For B2C sales through Steam or PlayStation Store where cash payment is accepted, the Cash Receipt System requires issuance of a cash receipt and transmission to HomeTax at the point of sale. There is no physical fiscal stamp or full blockchained real-time clearance system, but the HomeTax digital invoice registry operates as the statutory anti-fraud fiscal clearance infrastructure.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, 0% VAT applies to (i) goods exported by leaving the Korean customs territory under an accepted customs export declaration and (ii) services supplied to non-residents, non-domiciled persons, or foreign exchange-earning service transactions performed overseas. For Yuhan Hoesa PC and console game publication, digital game licenses and downloadable software transferred to Valve Steam, PlayStation Store, or directly to non-resident end customers qualify as zero-rated export services or export of digital goods only if the customer is a non-resident person, the service is not consumed in Korea, the consideration is received from a foreign payer in foreign currency, and the transaction is evidenced in Steam/PlayStation payout reports. Sales to Korean end users through domestic storefronts or local platform branches remain domestic supplies taxable at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Accepted KCS Export Declaration (UNI-PASS export declaration acceptance document and export performance confirmation), required only for physical game discs, collector editions, or hardware crossing the Korean customs border; not required for pure digital download supplies.

Steamworks payout report or PlayStation Store sales and payout statement identifying the non-resident contracting entity, the gross game license consideration, and the underlying digital distribution contract.

Foreign Exchange Bank Certificate of Received Export Proceeds issued under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (the Korean statutory equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate or FIRC) showing the matching foreign currency credit received in Korea from Steam, Valve, PlayStation, or the foreign buying platform.

Commercial invoice and, where physical goods are exported, Bill of Lading or Air Waybill; for digital exports, the corresponding SWIFT/MT103 credit advice or foreign exchange purchase contract showing conversion to KRW.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS will disallow zero-rating if the foreign recipient, place of supply, contract, performance, or foreign-exchange receipt is not contemporaneously documented. The supply will be recharacterized as taxable at 10%, unpaid VAT will be assessed with statutory interest, and additional tax will be imposed: generally 10% of the underpaid VAT for negligent underpayment, up to 20% for non-filing or unfounded refund claims, and up to 40% with criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for intentional false e-tax invoices, forged export declarations, or fraudulent export refunds. Already refunded input VAT is retrospectively clawed back with interest. The statutory assessment period is five years from the filing due date, extended to ten years for deliberate concealment or false documentation; a criminal tax fraud conviction removes the ordinary limitation period for recovery of the fraudulently obtained refund.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea, together with the Ministry of Strategy and Finance and the Foreign Exchange Information System administered under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a free-floating exchange rate regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is fully convertible for current account transactions such as software licensing, digital game publishing, royalty payments, and platform payouts, provided the underlying real economic transaction is documented and a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank files the required trade declaration. Capital account transactions are largely liberalized but remain subject to notification or reporting for foreign direct investment, cross-border loans, securities, and derivatives. Export proceeds do not have to be surrendered to the central bank; exporters may retain 100% of foreign currency receipts in designated foreign currency accounts or convert them to KRW at their bank. Profit remittances by a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa require board-authorized dividend minutes, audited financial statements, withholding tax payment confirmations, and a bank-filed foreign exchange declaration. The administration of FX controls is therefore transparent but compliance-documentation intensive. Domestic banks require purpose-of-payment codes for all wires, robust beneficial ownership files, confirmation that the transaction has a real underlying commercial contract, and sanctions screening. Profit repatriation is legally unrestricted for current account profits, yet the foreign investor must hold a valid report of foreign direct investment or the remittance may be suspended pending additional review. Practical hurdles are mainly KYC topicality, beneficial ownership transparency, source-of-funds evidence, and exact classification of the payment purpose under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act rather than quantitative convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds in Korea must be collected within 90 days of the export date unless a longer payment term is approved by a licensed foreign exchange bank due to commercial requirements. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; 100% of export proceeds may be retained in a foreign currency account and converted to KRW only as the exporter elects. The exporter must file receipt confirmation with the attestation institution and submit evidence of collection when the proceeds are credited to the foreign currency account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency and KRW Operational Account
USD Settlement and Foreign Direct Investment Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Overseas fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not licensed deposit-taking banks or authorized foreign exchange banks in South Korea and cannot legally provide KRW account servicing, KRW IBANs, or primary cross-border payment clearing for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa. An offshore EMI may act only as an ancillary receivable channel if it partners with a licensed Korean commercial bank, but regulatory exposure remains too high for core treasury operations. The corporate treasury must place all KRW and foreign currency clearing through Tier-1 domestic banks; using an unlicensed EMI for Steam or PlayStation payouts creates automatic AML and FX declaration failures.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South Korean banks generally require at least one statutory director or duly appointed legal representative with an apostilled board resolution to appear physically in a domestic branch for identity verification and the initial corporate KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening is rarely accepted by Tier-1 banks unless the foreign director has already been certified through correspondent banking and the bank acquires a full know-your-customer dossier. Subsequent signers may be added through power of attorney after the account is opened, but the first account signatory and the ultimate beneficial owner must satisfy face-to-face identity verification or a bank-approved video KYC process only where the bank explicitly permits it under its remote financial services compliance procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership sits through an opaque non-resident holding company with no economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full share register, apostilled memorandum of association, certificates of good standing from every jurisdiction in the ownership chain, a group structure chart showing all natural persons with 25% or greater interest, valid passport copies of each ultimate beneficial owner, independent electronic identity verification reports, audited financial statements of the parent entity, and signed declarations of source of wealth and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue stream from Steam and PlayStation digital stores looks inconsistent with the declared software publishing business scope
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Steam Partner Agreement and PlayStation Partner Agreement, platform payment policies, monthly gross revenue statements from Valve and Sony, developer or publisher distribution annexes, localized content development reports, VAT and digital services tax registrations, and invoices matching each inbound platform payout amount.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound remittances may be misclassified as investment capital instead of digital publishing royalties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board minutes approving the remittance, the signed publishing or intellectual property license agreement, the original remitter bank account statement, a correctly declared purpose-of-payment code, the KOTRA foreign direct investment report or foreign exchange bank notification, receipt certificate, and an external legal opinion confirming the cross-border transaction has an underlying commercial contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and embargo risk because digital game sales can reach jurisdictions subject to international or Korean sanctions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Geo-IP block policy excluding all comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions, platform confirmations of export-control exclusions, latest OFAC, EU, UN and Korean FSS sanctions screening results, customer lists backed by geo-gating evidence, an internal trade compliance manual, and an annual AML risk assessment prepared by a certified compliance consultant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections from foreign shareholders must be routed through a licensed domestic Korean foreign exchange bank after registering the foreign direct investment with the Ministry of Strategy and Finance and the receiving bank's foreign exchange system. The remitter must transfer funds via SWIFT MT103 with a precise payment narrative referencing the foreign direct investment report number, the ultimate beneficial owner, the Yuhan Hoesa corporate name, and the purpose of remittance as equity contribution. Upon crediting the capital escrow account, the bank issues a certificate of receipt and the capital verification is completed by matching the CFR code with the shareholder ledger. If funds are software royalty or platform advances, the payment purpose must be classified under the applicable current account code and supported by a written agreement and invoice before the bank releases funds into the operational KRW account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements for trade and non-trade services will use SWIFT MT103 clearing as the primary settlement rail for royalty payments, localization vendor fees, Steam platform aggregations, and consultant invoices. For tangible goods that require physical shipment, a commercial letter of credit may be used through a Korean Tier-1 bank, while documentary collections remain acceptable for lower-value physical deliverables. MT103 must include the beneficiary bank identifier, correspondent bank routing, and precise purpose code per the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The treasury function should never rely on peer-to-peer crypto rails or informal clearing houses for outbound commercial settlements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright KRW/USD forward contracts with a licensed Korean commercial bank, limited to one-year tenor and supported by underlying commercial exposure documentation
KRW/EUR forward contracts backed by verified European Steam and PlayStation payout settlements
Non-deliverable forward contracts using the Seoul closing won rate when the counterparty requires USD or EUR settlement outside Korea
Cross-currency swaps restricted to real cash-flow matching and approved by the bank's FX compliance desk under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Return and Local Income Tax Surtax Return, including annual financial statements, general ledger and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; the 10% local income tax surtax is included in the same filing and settled with the competent local government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 March of the following year, or 30 April if the return is prepared and signed by a licensed Korean tax agent (extension approved under NTS rules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late non-filing penalty of 20% of the assessed tax, understatement penalty of 10%, negligent understatement additional charge, and unpaid tax daily interest of 0.022% per day (i.e. 8.03% per annum). Repeated default gives the NTS the right to seize assets, cancel the business registration, and request court appointment of a liquidator; two consecutive years without filing and no business activity may trigger administrative strike-off and dissolution of the Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act and Framework Act on National Taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax (VAT) First Periodic Return and Preliminary/Periodic Payment for January through June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Semi-annual statutory filing due by 25 July for the first half (January-June) of the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled VAT penalty of 20% of the VAT payable, negligent underreporting penalty of 10%, and daily late-payment interest of 0.022%; persistent delinquency can disqualify input VAT credits, prompt a tax lien and business registration cancellation, and result in criminal fines under the Value-Added Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax (VAT) Second Periodic Return and Annual Aggregate VAT Settlement for July through December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Semi-annual statutory filing due by 25 January of the following year for the second half (July-December) of the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and tax non-declaration penalties apply at 20% of the net VAT payable, 10% for understated amounts, plus 0.022% daily interest on unpaid amounts; continuous failure may terminate the business registration and support criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements Filing (mandatory only if statutory thresholds are met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) DART system; copy retained at the registered office and presented to the members, creditors and the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants as required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months from fiscal year-end (by 31 March for a 31 December year-end), and the final audit report must be delivered to the FSS within two weeks after the annual members' meeting where the audited financial statements are approved; if no annual meeting is required for the LLC, no later than 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-appointment of a statutory auditor can change the audit to a FSS-designated independent auditor, and an FSS administrative penalty of up to KRW 30 million may be imposed; late filing of audited financial statements may incur a non-compliance fine; knowingly false audit reporting can expose responsible directors and the CPA to criminal sanctions under the External Audit Act and Capital Market Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner (UBO) and Membership Confirmation Record; Foreign-Investment Status Report (applicable to foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) via Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and local District Court Commercial Registration Division where a member change is registrable; the signed UBO confirmation is kept in the company's minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For foreign-invested entities: annual foreign-investment status report must be made to MOTIE by 30 June of each calendar year. All direct/indirect transfers of members' interests or UBO changes must be recorded in the statutory members' register and, if registrable, filed with the local Court Registry within 30 days of the event. The annual UBO confirmation must be completed no later than 31 March each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the foreign-investment status report or a registrable change triggers administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, loss of foreign-investment protection/tax benefits, and a non-compliance fine when a change is registered late at the Court Registration Office; repeated omissions may lead the Court to strike the registrable change and impose a per-day delay penalty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Secretarial Review: statutory registers, minute book, seal/certificate verification, and commercial registration file health check
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local County/District Court Commercial Registration Division and the National Tax Service business-registration file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the preparation of the CIT return and never later than 31 March of the following year; a real-time check is required within 14 days before each members' meeting or special resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Maintaining incomplete statutory registers or failing to file a registrable resolution is punishable by an non-compliance fine of up to KRW 5 million under Article 635 of the Korean Commercial Act; untimely disclosure to the Court can lead to rejection of registration, nominal fines, and, if the company fails to cure after two warning letters, administrative closure of the corporate registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa (LLC), an independent certified public accountant audit is statutorily mandatory under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree (applied by extension to limited liability companies) when any of the following is present at the end of the fiscal year: (1) balance-sheet total assets equal or exceed KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.4 million); (2) total assets equal or exceed KRW 7 billion (approximately USD 5.2 million) concurrently with annual operating turnover equal or exceeding KRW 20 billion (approximately USD 14.8 million) and an average quarterly workforce of 100 or more employees; (3) the company is an audit-designated entity or is required to submit audited financial statements by the Financial Services Commission, a court, or a qualified shareholder/creditor petition; or (4) foreign-invested status and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act require an audited balance sheet to maintain FDI eligibility. A non-listed Yuhan Hoesa operating under ISIC 5820 with total assets below KRW 10 billion, revenue below KRW 20 billion and fewer than 100 employees is normally exempt from a mandatory CPA audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board for listed and mandatory-audit companies; non-listed, non-audit-mandated entities may use Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) or the SME General Accounting Standards. If the entity becomes audit-mandated, financial statements must be prepared under K-IFRS or K-GAAP consistently, as accepted by the external auditor and in conformity with the Act on External Audit. Books, underlying contracts, invoices and electronic game-store royalty statements must be retained for at least 7 years to support the annual CIT/VAT filings and any court-register inspection.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Yuhan Hoesa must maintain an internal UBO and membership register and update it within 30 days of any event causing a direct or indirect change in equity ownership, voting power, economic interest or control, including any transfer of a member's interest, repurchase, merger, or liquidation. An annual confirmation signed by the manager/directors and certified by the corporate secretarial partner must be placed in the minute book by 31 March each year. Under the Korean financial information and AML/CFT framework, beneficial ownership must be identified at the 10% voting/equity threshold. For a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa, the same 30-day rule applies to the MOTIE foreign-investment change report. Registrable corporate changes (e.g. appointment or removal of a director/manager, amendment of the memorandum, change of registered office, transfer of a member's interest when required by the memorandum) must be filed at the local District Court Commercial Registration Division; non-registrable UBO movements remain confirmed in the internal register and disclosed to the company's bank and payment partners.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 950 per annum for a standard Korean registered office/registered agent arrangement, including official correspondence handling and director address services; full-service annual corporate secretary and compliance retainer: USD 1,200 - USD 3,000
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500 - USD 22,000 for a certified mandatory external audit by a licensed Korean CPA firm; if no statutory audit threshold is met, a voluntary review or compilation by a registered tax/accounting firm typically ranges from USD 800 - USD 2,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.2% combined top statutory rate (22% national corporate income tax plus 10% local income tax surtax on the national tax liability)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory incentives under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act: R&D tax credits of up to 50% of qualifying software/game development expenditures; corporate tax holidays for foreign direct investment in Free Economic Zones and Foreign Investment Zones (up to 5 years 100% exemption and 50% reduction for the following 2 years); income reduction for technology commercialization; job-creation investment tax credits. No general patent box regime exists, but technology and software R&D expenses qualify for super-deduction/credit programs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Final Return (Form 12) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing system (www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31st yearend, the statutory due date is March 31st of the following year; one month extension may be granted to April 30th upon application with legitimate cause.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, legal name, head office address, and fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned Korean Yuhan Hoesa, disclose foreign ownership percentage, ultimate beneficial owner country, and the place of effective management. Failure to identify a foreign controlling shareholder may cause the Korean tax authority to treat the entity as a Korean tax resident and deny reduction of withholding under a shareholder tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from PC and console video game sales through Steam and PlayStation Store, including platform commissions, in-app purchases, and downloadable content
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross sales on an accrual basis; do not net out Steam or PlayStation Store fees from revenue. Platform commissions are deductible only if supported by contracts and transfer pricing documentation. Any unrecorded foreign-store payout creates an immediate omission with exposure to fraudulent-evasion surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 26 (Royalty and license fees paid to foreign related parties)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Game engine royalties, software license fees, trademark fees, and intercompany service charges paid to foreign affiliates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For payments to non-resident affiliates, characterize the payment in Korean source rules and withhold at the statutory rate unless a bilateral DTA reduced rate is substantiated. Provide a transfer pricing benchmark, local file, and beneficial ownership certificate for the recipient. Unsupported royalty payments are a primary transfer pricing red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating losses from prior years used to reduce current taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the loss carryforward only within the statutory 10-year window and only if audited financial records exist. A loss carryforward may be denied if an ownership change was effected to acquire tax losses rather than for bona fide business reasons. Non-resident directors must be aware of the Korean anti-trafficking loss limitation practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income after adjustments and special deductions, including foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When computing taxable income, apply the 10%-20%-22% national corporate tax schedule and local surtax. Cross-border intercompany adjustments must be compliant with OECD transfer pricing principles; the Korean tax authority may recharacterize abandoned erosion payments if the Korean entity lacks economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration required to support dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents during the tax year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before finalizing the return, verify whether dividend distributions to foreign shareholders have attracted 22% withholding tax. If treaty-reduced withholding is intended, attach the recipient's Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership certificate, and a declaration of actual substance; otherwise the withholding agent is personally liable for the deficiency.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failing to file the corporate tax return by the legal deadline triggers a non-declaration surcharge of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; filing a return with understated income triggers an understatement surcharge of 10% of the understated tax; fraudulent omission or evasion triggers a 40% surcharge. Late payment interest accrues at the statutory daily rate (approximately 0.022% per day) from the original due date until fully paid. If the evaded tax amount in a three-year period exceeds KRW 500 million, criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may result in imprisonment or fines and immediate restriction of departure (travel blacklist).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate withholding tax (20% national withholding under Corporate Tax Act Article 98 and 2% local income tax surtax under the Local Income Tax Act)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a bilateral double tax treaty reduction, the non-resident recipient must deliver to the Korean withholding agent before the taxable payment: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent tax authority of the residence state; (ii) a certificate or declaration of beneficial ownership stating that the recipient is the true owner and not a conduit; and (iii) documentation of actual business substance, including board appointment records and employment/office substance in the residence state. The withholding agent then applies the reduced rate on HomeTax. If the reduced rate is not applied at source, the non-resident may file a refund claim through the Korean National Tax Service within the statutory claim period. The Korean tax authority may deny treaty benefits under general anti-abuse, OECD MLI limitation-on-benefits, or principal purpose tests if the arrangement lacks commercial substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding rate for royalties and interest paid to non-residents is also 22% aggregate (20% national plus 2% local income tax). Treaty-reduced rates vary by country and instrument, commonly in the range of 10%-15% for dividends, interest, and royalties. Royalties for computer software, game IP, or trademarks attributable to use in Korea remain Korean-source income for withholding purposes. Interest on intercompany loans to the Korean entity is subject to withholding unless the DTA imposes a notional upper limit; the Korean tax authority may recharacterize excessive interest as a dividend under thin capitalization and transfer pricing rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Cross-border related-party transactions exceeding KRW 10 billion in a fiscal year trigger mandatory preparation and submission of transfer pricing documentation, including Local File and summaries of core transactions; Master File is required when the Korean entity is a constituent unit of a multinational group with aggregate annual consolidated revenue exceeding KRW 1 trillion, and Country-by-Country reporting applies to the ultimate parent at the same group threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply the UAE/Caribbean format of Economic Substances Regulations, but Korean tax law and tax treaty jurisprudence require actual commercial substance of a Korean entity. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa engaged in Steam and PlayStation publishing must have a substantive place of management, local board decisions, full-time employees exercising core income-generating activities, actual execution of contracts with rights holders, and bank accounts in Korea. Absence of these indicators can cause a foreign parent to be treated as having a Korean permanent establishment, or permit the tax authority to disregard the Korean entity as an artificial conduit under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs and OECD anti-abuse principles.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion under the Corporate Income Tax Law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean video game publisher intentionally omits digital store revenues from Steam and PlayStation, fabricates refunds or payout records, and shifts profit to a related offshore entity without legitimate commercial purpose, resulting in deliberate understatement of Korean corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, Article 3: imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or a criminal fine not exceeding five times the evaded tax; aggravated evasion of an amount exceeding KRW 500 million in a three-year period may lead to higher imprisonment terms. Additionally, the National Tax Service imposes a 40% fraudulent underreporting penalty plus local income tax, daily interest, and publication of non-compliant taxpayers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil can be pierced: directors who directed or participated in the concealment are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax, surcharges, interest, and civil restitution. Assets and bank accounts can be seized; the director and representative shareholder can be blacklisted and subject to a travel ban. Criminal imprisonment is the direct personal sanction for intentional evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Artificial Intercompany Pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean game publisher pays excessive royalties or platform commissions to a foreign related party without an arm's-length benchmark, omits the required transfer pricing documentation despite exceeding KRW 10 billion in related-party transactions, and uses a shell parent entity abroad merely to shift taxable profits away from Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, failure to submit or prepare transfer pricing documentation can trigger a penalty equal to 3% of the undisclosed international transaction amount, subject to statutory maximums; tax authorities may reallocate taxable income under the arm's-length principle, impose a 20% deficiency surcharge, assess daily late-payment interest, and deny foreign tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean tax collection rules permit the National Tax Service to collect the deficiency from a director or controlling shareholder where the corporate assets were dissipated before the assessment. If invoices, contracts, or Board minutes are falsified, the responsible director may face criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including imprisonment, and the court may pierce the veil to impose personal civil liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Non-Compliance and Treaty Relief Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity distributes dividends or pays royalties and interest to non-resident shareholders without deducting the 22% statutory withholding tax, or falsely claims a reduced treaty rate by relying on a stale or forged Tax Residency Certificate while the actual beneficial owner is not entitlement-holder, or disguises dividends as loan repayment to avoid withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act Article 98 and Local Income Tax Act Article 110 impose withholding obligations on the Korean payer; the withholding agent becomes personally liable for the unwithheld amount together with a 10% un-collected withholding penalty, interest, and a 20% understatement penalty where the failure was wrongful. Criminal fraud may be charged where the same act involves false or fake taxation documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign dividend resolutions or direct payment disbursements are statutory withholding agents and are jointly and severally liable for the shortfall. The tax authority may attach personal assets, impose a travel ban and blacklisting, and seek criminal imprisonment for intentional non-withholding. Civil claims for restitution of the unpaid dividends may also be brought against directors for breach of fiduciary duty and unjust enrichment.
